jobs.title: Data Scientist, Discovery & Recommendations
jobs.description:
**DESCRIPTION**
---------------

If you are interested in this position, please apply on Twitch's Career site https://www.twitch.tv/jobs/en/If you are interested in this position, please apply on Twitch's Career site https://www.twitch.tv/jobs/en/  
  
About Us  
Twitch is the world’s biggest live streaming service, with global communities built around gaming, entertainment, music, sports, cooking, and more. It is where thousands of communities come together for whatever, every day.  
We’re about community, inside and out. You’ll find coworkers who are eager to team up, collaborate, and smash (or elegantly solve) problems together. We’re on a quest to empower live communities, so if this sounds good to you, see what we’re up to on LinkedIn and X, and discover the projects we’re solving on our Blog. Be sure to explore our Interviewing Guide to learn how to ace our interview process.  
  
About the Role  
  
We're looking for a data scientist with strong statistics and modeling skills to be the science partner for the machine learning and recommendation systems behind Twitch's discovery products. You will work with product managers, ML engineers and applied scientists to help build what our recommendation systems should optimize for. That means balancing what a viewer does today (a click, a play, minutes watched) against what keeps them coming back: return visits, daily habits, and lasting connections with creators. It also means weighing short-form clips against long-form live content, and each surface against the others. This role will draw from a variety of statistical learning techniques, causal inference, optimization and recommender systems evaluation, and it still owns the full path from question to decision.  
  
  
Reporting to the Director of Data Science, you will work from our San Francisco, CA office.  
  
You Will  

* Help define the objective functions and success metrics for ranking and recommendations across feeds, search and notifications. Make the trade-offs explicit between short-term engagement (clicks, plays, watch time) and long-term outcomes (return visits, retention, new creator connections), including how short-form clips and live content add to or take away from each other.
* Evaluate ranking, recommendation and feed changes with ML engineers and applied scientists. This covers A/B tests and long-running holdouts, offline metrics that predict online results, and the cost and value of exploration and cold start. Handle the hard cases: novelty effects, interference between experiments, two-sided marketplace effects involving creators and viewers, and feedback loops in recommendation data.
* Build statistical and ML models that explain viewer behavior and size opportunities, such as propensity, uplift, survival and retention models. Include proxy metrics that predict long-term retention, so teams can decide in days rather than months.
* Turn ambiguous product questions into clear analyses. Quantify the uncertainty, and make recommendations that inform the machine learning and discovery roadmap.
* Define the logging and data needed to measure discovery surfaces, and check its quality.
* Contribute to the team's standards for experimentation, causal inference and model evaluation, and share what you learn with other data scientists.

  
Perks  

* Medical, Dental, Vision & Disability Insurance
* 401(k)
* Maternity & Parental Leave
* Flexible PTO
* Amazon Employee Discount

  
About the team  
Twitch is all about community, and our Community team is a core pillar of what makes Twitch, Twitch. Community Discovery & ML (CDML) helps millions of viewers find the creators and communities they'll love. That covers search, browse, the mobile live and clips feeds, recommended notifications, and the recommendation systems behind them. When a viewer finds a new creator through one of these, it's often the start of a lasting connection. That connection is what keeps viewers, and the creators they watch, coming back.

**BASIC QUALIFICATIONS**
------------------------

* 3+ years of data scientist experience
* A BA/BS in Statistics, Mathematics, Computer Science, Economics, Data Science or a related quantitative field, or equivalent industry experience.
* 3+ years as a data scientist in a high-velocity, data-driven environment, with hands-on experience applying statistical modeling and machine learning (regression, classification, causal inference, time series), including the assumptions behind each method and when it fails.
* Experience designing and analyzing online experiments, including variance reduction, power analysis and the pitfalls of interpreting results.
* Expert SQL and proficiency in Python or R.
* A track record of using data and models to influence product decisions and leadership.

**PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS**
----------------------------

* An MS or PhD in a quantitative field.
* Experience with recommender systems, search ranking or feed ranking, such as offline evaluation (precision and recall, NDCG), exploration versus exploitation, or cold-start problems.
* Experience with multi-objective optimization or with defining objective functions for ranking systems, including choosing weights between competing goals.
* Experience building proxy metrics for long-term outcomes, or estimating long-term effects from long-running holdouts or observational data (e.g., difference-in-differences, synthetic control, uplift modeling).
* Experience with two-sided platforms or marketplaces, where changes for viewers also affect creators or supply.
* Experience on a consumer content platform: streaming, short-form video, social or marketplaces.
* Familiarity with Twitch, as a viewer or a creator (or both!).

jobs.title: Applied Scientist II, Brand Optimization
jobs.description:
**DESCRIPTION**
---------------

Amazon Advertising is one of Amazon's fastest growing businesses, responsible for defining and delivering a collection of advertising products that drive discovery and sales. Brand advertising is at the center of that growth, and brand marketers are pushing the industry toward a fundamental shift: they no longer want to optimize toward proxy metrics like reach and frequency alone. They want their investment across Streaming TV, online video, and display to drive measurable business outcomes, from consideration through to purchase and long-term loyalty. The core scientific challenge is connecting a brand ad exposure today to an outcome that may happen days or weeks later, and then optimizing for it in real time.  
  
The Brand Outcomes Optimization team exists to solve that challenge. We build machine-learned models that predict how likely a customer is to move along the full funnel, from awareness through conversion, and we integrate those predictions into real-time bidding so that every brand bid is placed on the opportunity most likely to produce the outcome the advertiser cares about. These systems operate at large scale, and even small improvements to how we predict and optimize for outcomes have meaningful and immediate impact on advertiser results.  
  
As an Applied Scientist II, you will help drive this outcome-optimization. You will take on increasingly ambiguous problems, from predicting what a brand outcome will be, to building the bidding and control algorithms that optimize for it, to proving the lift through experimentation. You will work alongside senior scientists and engineers, applying advances in machine learning, online optimization, optimal control, forecasting, and causal inference. You will also join the Amazon science community, with opportunities to publish papers, attend workshops and conferences, and gain early access to Amazon ML technologies.  
  
Key job responsibilities  
In this role, you will work with a highly motivated team of ML scientists and engineers focused on making brand advertising measurable and optimizable against real outcomes. As an Applied Scientist II, you will:  
  

* Contribute to outcome-driven brand optimization, helping define, predict, and bid toward brand outcomes across channels.
* Build prediction models that estimate a customer's likelihood to progress through the funnel, and integrate them into bidding systems.
* Develop the optimization and control algorithms that turn outcome predictions into bids.
* Own projects end to end: frame the problem and success metrics, build and validate prototypes, partner with engineers to productionize, and prove impact through offline analysis and online A/B experimentation.
* Help establish scalable, automated processes for training, monitoring, and feedback so outcome optimization stays reliable and performant at scale.
* Contribute to the science bar on the team through design and model reviews.

**BASIC QUALIFICATIONS**
------------------------

* 3+ years of building models for business application experience
* PhD, or Master's degree and 4+ years of CS, CE, ML or related field experience
* Experience programming in Java, C++, Python or related language
* Experience in designing experiments and statistical analysis of results

**PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS**
----------------------------

* Experience in state-of-the-art deep learning models architecture design and deep learning training and optimization and model pruning

* Experience building or maintaining data pipelines at scale. Spark, Databricks, Delta Lake, or equivalent.

jobs.title: Engineer - MLOps & Scientific Platforms - Data Foundry
jobs.description:
At Lilly, the work is demanding because patients are waiting. We unite caring with discovery to help make life better for people around the world, knowing that every decision, every detail, and every day matters. Headquartered in Indianapolis, Indiana, our over 50,000 employees around the globe take on complex challenges to discover and deliver life-changing medicines, strengthen how health is understood and managed, and support the communities we serve. This is hard, urgent, selfless work—but it’s work worth doing. If you’re driven by purpose and ready to bring your best to work that truly matters for patients, we invite you to join us.
  
  
**Locations:** San Francisco, CA; Louisville, CO; Indianapolis, IN
  
  
Lilly Small Molecule Discovery is purpose-built to create molecules that make life better for people. Discovery Technology and Platforms (DTP) accelerates molecule discovery by building optimized foundational platforms, streamlining lab operations through advanced technologies and data connectivity, and investing in novel capabilities.
  
Data Foundry is a multidisciplinary team within DTP that enables AI-native drug discovery through four integrated pillars: Architecture4Insight (data infrastructure and scientific software), Methods4Insight (analytical and computational methods), Automation & Scale4Insight (lab automation and agentic workflows), and Preparedness4Insight (data governance and readiness). These pillars empower every Lilly scientist to make optimal decisions by providing seamless access to data, insights, and AI-driven capabilities—serving both human scientists and autonomous AI agents.
  
  
Position Summary
  
  
We are seeking an Engineer - MLOps & Scientific Platforms - Data Foundry to operationalize Data Foundry’s scientific tools and analytical methods into actionable-prototypes. You will build the ML deployment pipelines, model serving infrastructure, API layers, and observability guardrails that make our scientific discovery methods and tools reliable, scalable, and consumable, both by discovery scientists and by the Frontier AI group’s autonomous agents.
  
This role sits at the interface between Methods4Insight (which develops analytical methods) and Architecture4Insight(which provides the agile data infrastructure). Your job is to ensure every scientific tool Data Foundry produces are analytics-ready, well-monitored, and exposed through APIs with the response-time guarantees and error handling that both human users and AI agents require.
  
  
Responsibilities
  
  
MLOps & Model Lifecycle Management
  
  

* Build and maintain end-to-end ML deployment pipelines: experiment tracking, model versioning (MLflow, Weights & Biases), containerized model serving, and automated retraining triggers.
* Develop model registry infrastructure and feature engineering pipelines that enable computational scientists to access models.
* Implement monitoring and alerting for data pipelines, APIs, ML models, and agentic systems (LLMOps) to ensure system reliability and performance at scale.
* Build dashboards and metrics tracking for pipeline execution, API latency, token usage, model prediction quality, and system health

* Collaborate with EC2 teams and manufacturing partners to ensure smooth system integration
* Drive end-to-end qualification processes for new software implementations

You'll design and develop the software and firmware that drives NeuronSwitches- the high-performance interconnect fabric for Trainium chips. jobs.title: Postdoctoral Fellow Computational Biology and Machine Learning, Jhunjhunwala Lab
jobs.description:
### **The Position**

Why Genentech

  
  

A healthier future. It’s what drives us to innovate. To continuously advance science and ensure everyone has access to the healthcare they need today and for generations to come. Creating a world where we all have more time with the people we love. That’s what makes us Genentech.

  
  

We are seeking a machine learning scientist to join our Computational Sciences Center of Excellence as a Postdoctoral Fellow. In this role, you will apply advanced ML techniques to disease biology to significantly impact our understanding of disease biology and the discovery of novel therapeutic interventions. A successful candidate will conduct cutting-edge research at the intersection of machine learning, biology, and drug development. This position offers a unique opportunity to be jointly mentored by experienced machine learning and computational scientists, with close collaboration across Genentech’s research organization.

  
  

**The Opportunity:**

The primary focus of this role is developing deep learning models for multimodal cellular data to decode cell differentiation and predict how interventions alter cellular phenotypes. Specifically, you will build deep representations of T cell biology to better understand T cell differentiation and various phenotypic states from a therapeutic perspective. Leveraging a strong background in machine learning and hands-on experience with deep learning architectures, your research responsibilities will include designing, training, and evaluating generative and conditional models, including transformer-based architectures. In this role, you will collaborate closely with computational and experimental scientists to generate and test biological hypotheses directly relevant to drug discovery.

  
  

This is a fantastic opportunity to contribute to world-class science in a leading biotechnology company.

  
  

**Who You Are:**

  
  

* PhD in Machine Learning, Computer Science, Statistics, Applied Mathematics, Computational Science, or a related field, with a strong focus on machine learning methods development.
* Impactful researcher with first-author publications in leading scientific journals or main tracks in top-tier machine learning conferences.
* Strong hands-on experience designing, training, and evaluating deep learning architectures, with particular interest in experience developing generative models or models for conditional prediction.
* Strong programming skills in Python, PyTorch, and higher-level libraries (such as huggingface), with experience implementing custom model components and training workflows.
* Pragmatic and focused researcher, driven to solve complex scientific problems independently and in a collaborative environment.
* Excellent oral and written communication skills, with the ability to communicate across machine learning and biological disciplines.
  

  

**Preferred Qualifications**

* Experience with generative transformers
* Developing models for single-cell or multimodal biological data.
* Strong understanding of multi-omics and NGS data
* Experience in immunology and T cell biology is a plus.
  

  

For information about the Jhunjhunwala Lab at Genentech, please go to:

https://www.gene.com/scientists/our-scientists/suchit-jhunjhunwala

  
  

**Relevant publications:**

* Theodoris, C. V. et al. Transfer learning enables predictions in network biology. Nature 618, 616–624 (2023).
* Cui, H. et al. scGPT: toward building a foundation model for single-cell multi-omics using generative AI. Nature Methods 21, 1470–1480 (2024).
* Levine, D. et al. Cell2Sentence: Teaching Large Language Models the Language of Biology. Proceedings of the 41st International Conference on Machine Learning, PMLR 235, 27299–27325 (2024).
* Lopez, R. et al. Deep generative modeling for single-cell transcriptomics. Nature Methods 15, 1053–1058 (2018).
* Roohani, Y. et al. Predicting transcriptional outcomes of novel multigene perturbations with GEARS. Nature Biotechnology 42, 927–935 (2024).
* Lotfollahi, M. et al. Predicting cellular responses to complex perturbations in high-throughput screens. Molecular Systems Biology 19, e11517 (2023).

jobs.title: Forward Deployed Engineer, Defense
jobs.description:
Navi captures everything a pilot sees and hears and turns it into automated debrief intelligence, sortie-level awareness that has never existed before. You're building the platform that makes that happen.

Navi is live at the U.S. Air Force Test Pilot School, Embry-Riddle, United Aviate, Sling Pilot Academy and Delta State University. You'll take it to the next squadron, the next schoolhouse and the next aircraft.

**On site with customers 30 to 50% of the time · U.S. citizenship required**

**About the role**
==================

In a military flying unit, Navi is the data off every sortie, a debrief waiting when the crew walks in, and the picture instructors and commanders run training, readiness and safety on. Forward deployed engineers make that work at each unit.

You'll spend real time on base with aircrew, instructors, maintainers and commanders. Then you'll write the production code that turns what you learned into product. Not a prototype, not a slide deck: the same codebase every customer runs. You'll own a deployment end to end, from the data coming off the aircraft to the people acting on it.

**Problems you'll own**
=======================

**Get the data off the aircraft.** A sortie lands as recorder files, mission data cartridges, cockpit video and audio, sitting on government computers and removable media. Each has its own format, sampling rate and clock, and its own traps: a time code with no year, a clock that was never set, an altitude that follows the altimeter setting. You'll build the converters and the uploader that runs unattended on an operations desk, and line every source up to the same instant.

**Make the debrief one an instructor would sign.** A unit's training lives in syllabi, gradesheets, maneuver guides and instructor standards. You'll turn those into events, tolerances and rubrics a sortie can be held to, and build the tools instructors use to keep them current. Then you'll prove it works: grades checked against the instructors' own, and every finding tied to the data and the document behind it.

**Build what commanders run the unit on.** Where each student stands in the syllabus and who is falling behind, upcoming evaluations and checkrides, instructor workload, aircraft availability. You'll find the question a squadron commander or director of operations asks every week and make Navi answer it.

**See safety across the whole fleet.** Every exceedance, unstable approach and trend across every sortie, not only the ones someone wrote up. You'll turn flight data into a safety picture a unit can act on before something happens.

**Put the unit's knowledge one question away.** Regulations, syllabi, maneuver guides and lessons learned are spread across hundreds of documents. You'll build the assistant that answers from them and from the unit's own flight data, with a citation behind every answer.

**Deploy where the mission is.** Controlled unclassified information, restricted networks, government computers without admin rights, older hardware, MFA, audit trails and accreditation. You'll build to those constraints from day one, make a 3D replay run smoothly on a five-year-old government laptop, and help write the security documentation that goes with it.

**Close the loop.** Aircrew and instructors rate debriefs, flag findings and correct transcripts. You'll turn that into fixes that ship the same week, and into patterns the product team builds for every customer.

**About you**
=============

* 3+ years shipping production software, in any programming language. You've owned a system in production end to end.
* You're at home in messy real-world data: file formats, sampling rates, clock alignment, units, sensor faults, missing channels.
* Comfortable below the application. You can stand up an environment, read an access policy and debug a service that won't start.
* You can sit with aircrew, an instructor or a commander and come back with the right problem, not just the one they named.
* You build with AI coding agents every day, and you know how to check their work: tests, measurements and a second look before anything ships.
* You're comfortable owning outcomes when the roadmap isn't written yet.
* U.S. citizen, able to travel to bases regularly.

**Nice to have**
================

* Military aviation experience: aircrew, instructor, maintainer, flight test or safety
* Flight training or standardization and evaluation (Stan/Eval) in a flying unit
* Military flight data: mission data recorders, IRIG time code, IRIG 106 Chapter 10, MIL-STD-1553
* Aviation safety programs such as MFOQA
* Security and accreditation work: NIST 800-171, CMMC, RMF or an ATO package
* An active security clearance
* Signal processing, computer vision on cockpit video, or speech-to-text on cockpit audio

**What this role is not**
=========================

Not a sales engineer running demos. Not support working a ticket queue. Not a consultant handing over a report. You write production code that ships to every customer, and you're the reason it works where it lands.

**Why this role matters**
=========================

Every sortie is expensive, and much of what it records is never reviewed. Navi turns each one into a debrief in about a minute and puts what a unit learns in front of the people who make decisions about aircrew, aircraft and safety. The bar is a debrief an instructor would sign and a picture a commander would act on. As the engineer in the room, you're the one who gets it there.

**What you'll get**
===================

* Early-stage equity: real ownership in a category-defining company
* Flight training: earn your pilot's license and build with true domain expertise
* Time on the flight line with the people who use what you build
* A role that grows into leading Navi's defense engineering as we scale

jobs.title: Product Engineer - Onboarding Automation
jobs.description:
**About Stuut**
===============

Stuut is the AI coworker that runs order-to-cash for the world’s leading enterprises. Across order management, credit, collections, payments, cash application, disputes and deductions, Stuut does the work end to end and keeps going until the cash hits the bank.

Over 150 companies, spanning the mid-market to the Fortune 50, including Honeywell, ZoomInfo and PerkinElmer, use Stuut to unlock up to 40% more cash flow and cut DSO by 47%. More than $3 billion has moved through the platform to date.

Founded in New York by Tarek Alaruri and Ben Winter, Stuut has raised $93 million from Insight Partners, Andreessen Horowitz, M12, Microsoft’s Venture Fund, and others. Learn more at stuut.ai.

**The Role**
------------

We're hiring our first Product Engineer dedicated to customer onboarding. Your job is to make bringing a new customer live on Stuut faster and smoother, and to build the tools our Forward Deployed Engineering (FDE) team uses on every implementation.

Every new customer brings its own ERP, data, email templates, and collections process. You'll work alongside our FDEs, find the steps that can be automated, and ship the tools that make each onboarding faster than the last: a smarter intake form and the APIs behind it, and agents that turn a customer's existing collateral into a configured account.

This work also lays the foundation for channel partners to implement Stuut for their own clients.

**What Success Looks Like**
---------------------------

Within your first quarter, you've shipped an onboarding automation used on live customers. Within 12 months, customers go live meaningfully faster, your tooling is a core part of every implementation, and it's robust enough for channel partners to use.

**What You'll Do**
------------------

* **Build the intake-to-configuration path:** Turn our intake form into a full product, with the APIs behind it so customer inputs configure an account end to end.
* **Ship agents for onboarding:** Build LLM-powered tools that turn customer collateral (email templates, collection playbooks, process docs) into working Stuut configuration.
* **Make customer data easy:** Make ERP data, flat-file, and schema mapping fast and reliable, whether that means building or integrating the right tool.
* **Improve the onboarding toolkit:** Continuously improve the tools and automation our FDEs use on every implementation.
* **Find the bottleneck, ship the simple fix:** Work with FDEs and customers, measure where time goes, and ship the smallest thing that moves it before building the big thing.
* **Build for partners:** Design onboarding tooling that channel partners can use too.
* **Build with agents:** Use coding agents daily to ship quickly, while owning the testing and debugging of what they produce.

**You Might Be a Fit If You…**
------------------------------

* **Ship real LLM features:** You've built agents, tool use, and prompt/eval loops that run in production, not just demos.
* **Build APIs and backends:** You're comfortable designing APIs that take structured input and configure a system end to end, in a large existing codebase.
* **Handle messy data:** You've worked with ERP data, flat files, schema mapping, validation, and cleaning. ETL experience is a plus.
* **Have product sense:** You can talk to internal users and customers, find the biggest bottleneck, and ship the simplest fix first.
* **Work autonomously:** You scope your own projects once given priorities, and you're comfortable being the first person in a function that may grow into a team.
* **Work agent-native:** You use coding agents every day and can explain and stand behind their output.

**Suggested background:** 5+ years as a software engineer, with time in backend, full-stack, or forward deployed roles at a B2B SaaS or fintech company. We weigh shipped work and judgment over any specific title.

**Bonus Points**
----------------

* You've worked as a forward deployed, implementation, or solutions engineer.
* You've built B2B SaaS onboarding, or worked in fintech, AR/AP, or ERP.
* You've built tools that partners or customers use to implement a product themselves.

**US Compensation**

* Top-of-market salary and equity package
* Benefits (for U.S.-based full-time employees)
* Medical, dental & vision insurance coverage for you
* 401(k) & Match
* Equity
* Flexible PTO
* Parental Leave

We do not discriminate based on race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, national origin, age, disability, veteran status, genetic information, or any other characteristic protected by applicable law.**

jobs.title: Inference Infrastructure Engineer
jobs.description:
**The role**
============

As an inference infrastructure engineer, you’ll build and operate the systems that deploy Applied Compute’s models and serve production inference traffic. You’ll own model deployment, GPU capacity management, request routing, and recovery from failures, balancing reliability, latency, and serving efficiency. You’ll partner with research engineers to support new models and with inference performance engineers to bring execution improvements into production. Your work will make it possible to release models safely, securely, and serve changing workloads reliably.

**What You’ll Do**

* Design, build, and maintain the inference APIs developers use to interact with our models, supporting streaming responses, tool use, structured outputs, and multimodal inputs.
* Build services that take model checkpoints through deployment, health checks, staged rollout, and rollback. Give engineers a dependable way to launch endpoints, inspect their behavior, and update model versions or configurations.
* Develop GPU placement and autoscaling systems that account for model memory requirements, startup time, hardware availability, and changing demand.
* Build routing, queueing, and admission-control policies that balance latency, throughput, and GPU utilization while maintaining isolation between workloads and protecting the service from overload.
* Make deployments resilient to failed processes, unhealthy GPUs, and unavailable hosts through failure detection, recovery, and replacement.
* Establish service objectives, telemetry, and load tests that make serving behavior understandable. Investigate incidents across service code, model servers, networking, and cluster resources, and turn recurring failures into lasting fixes.
* Partner with inference performance engineers to evaluate serving configurations under representative traffic and safely deploy improvements without disrupting active workloads.

**What We’re Looking For**

* Strong software engineering skills and experience building and maintaining backend services or distributed systems in production.
* Proficiency in Go, Rust, Python, C++, or a comparable language, with the ability to navigate unfamiliar code and make well-tested changes.
* Experience designing systems that coordinate work across multiple machines, including an understanding of concurrency, state management, and partial failures.
* Good judgment about queueing, timeouts, retries, backpressure, and resource isolation, and how these choices affect a service under load.
* Practical knowledge of Linux, containers, and cloud infrastructure. You can investigate problems that cross software and infrastructure boundaries.
* Experience supporting software after release: diagnosing incidents, improving monitoring, and making changes safely while users depend on the service.
* Ownership and clear technical communication: you can work through open-ended problems, use measurements to guide decisions, explain tradeoffs, and stay accountable for the result after release.

We welcome strong backend and distributed systems engineers who are moving into inference. Prior experience with model serving or GPU infrastructure is helpful, but not required.

**Nice to Have**

* Experience managing accelerator fleets or supporting inference workloads with changing model sizes, traffic patterns, and hardware requirements.
* Familiarity with model-serving fundamentals, including GPU memory constraints, model loading, and the different resource demands of prefill and decode.
* Experience deploying or operating serving engines such as vLLM, SGLang, or TensorRT-LLM.
* Experience extending Kubernetes through controllers or building software for workload placement and capacity management.
* Familiarity with GPU health diagnostics, high-speed interconnects, or inference deployments that span multiple machines.
* Experience building foundational infrastructure at an early-stage company or contributing to open-source systems software.

The U.S. base salary range for this full-time position is 275-400k. Total compensation includes equity and a comprehensive benefits package. Individual compensation depends on qualifications, experience, skills, and work location.

**Benefits & Logistics**
========================

This role is based in San Francisco. We work from our office in the Mission. We offer:

* Competitive compensation and equity
* 100% employer-paid health insurance coverage for you and your family
* Unlimited PTO

* Daily lunches and dinners

jobs.title: Forward Deployed Engineer, Evals
jobs.description:
**About David AI**
------------------

At David AI, our vision is to bring impactful AI into billions of lives through voice. Our mission is to help the world's leading AI companies build better voice models and agents. We're building the data and evaluation infrastructure behind those models.

Founded in 2024, we're a fast-growing Series B company backed by NVIDIA, Meritech, First Round, YC, and others, with ~70 people across San Francisco and New York City.

**About this role**
-------------------

We're building David AI's first **Forward Deployed Evals** team. Voice models can only improve on what someone can measure, and most of what matters in voice has never been measured well. This team finds those gaps with our customers and builds the evals to close them.

As a **Forward Deployed Engineer, Evals**, you'll be the primary partner to a set of customers' research teams. In a typical week, you might spot a regression in the latest model checkpoint and design a targeted eval for it, build it end-to-end, calibrate findings against human ratings, and follow through to ensure the model improves.

This is a builder role that is intentionally cross-functional, requiring you to be capable across GTM, Ops, Product, Research, and Engineering to deliver on outcomes.

**In this role, you will**
--------------------------

* Be the evaluation partner to research teams at the world's leading AI labs: learn what they're trying to fix in their voice models, and find what they haven't thought to measure yet.
* Dig into human and automated eval results, pin down exactly where and why a model fails, and decide which failures deserve a dedicated eval.
* Go from idea to working eval in days, independently building whatever the problem calls for: human data pipelines, detectors trained on human labels, or synthetic test harnesses.
* Make every number defensible: an eval you ship should track what people actually hear, and it should hold up when a senior researcher pushes on it.
* Tell research leads what to focus on in their next checkpoint and why, with the data to back it up.
* Productize what works, or turn it into a playbook the team can repeat.
* Shape how forward deployed evals work at David AI as one of the first people on the team.

**Your background looks like**
------------------------------

* 2-7+ years of experience as a technical builder across engineering, product, operations, and research (we're hiring at multiple levels); this might have been as a forward deployed engineer, applied data scientist, ML engineer, product manager, management consultant, or something else entirely.
* You're exceptional at building with AI agents, and you've personally built at least one ambitious thing you can walk us through in detail.
* You move fast. You solve problems in days that might take someone else a month, and you own ambiguous, high-stakes work end to end.
* Strong, demonstrated analytical chops: experiment design, statistics, and knowing whether a metric actually captures what you care about.
* Strong customer presence: you have the credibility and clear communication to earn the trust of technical customers and senior stakeholders.
* Excited to work in person in San Francisco or New York.

**Bonus points if you have**
----------------------------

* Been a founder, or founding engineer/PM/etc. at a startup.
* Experience with speech, audio, or voice models.
* Built or published a benchmark you can share with us.
* Experience working with human raters, annotation, or data-labeling workflows.
* Worked at an AI data or evals company.

**Benefits**
------------

* Unlimited PTO.
* Top-notch health, dental, and vision coverage with 100% coverage for most plans.
* FSA & HSA access.
* 401k access.
* Meals 2x daily through DoorDash + snacks and beverages available at the office.
* Unlimited company-sponsored Barry's classes.

**Visas**
---------

We sponsor international candidates across several visa types, including H-1B *transfers*, H-1B1, O-1, E-3, and TN. We also hire candidates on STEM OPT. If you’re on STEM OPT, we’ll want to confirm you have a path to one of the visas listed above before your OPT ends. While we can’t guarantee any individual outcome, we’ve successfully sponsored teammates from all over the world.

jobs.title: Applied Scientist II, Brand Optimization
jobs.description:
**DESCRIPTION**
---------------

Amazon Advertising is one of Amazon's fastest growing businesses, responsible for defining and delivering a collection of advertising products that drive discovery and sales. Brand advertising is at the center of that growth, and brand marketers are pushing the industry toward a fundamental shift: they no longer want to optimize toward proxy metrics like reach and frequency alone. They want their investment across Streaming TV, online video, and display to drive measurable business outcomes, from consideration through to purchase and long-term loyalty. The core scientific challenge is connecting a brand ad exposure today to an outcome that may happen days or weeks later, and then optimizing for it in real time.  
  
The Brand Outcomes Optimization team exists to solve that challenge. We build machine-learned models that predict how likely a customer is to move along the full funnel, from awareness through conversion, and we integrate those predictions into real-time bidding so that every brand bid is placed on the opportunity most likely to produce the outcome the advertiser cares about. These systems operate at large scale, and even small improvements to how we predict and optimize for outcomes have meaningful and immediate impact on advertiser results.  
  
As an Applied Scientist II, you will help drive this outcome-optimization. You will take on increasingly ambiguous problems, from predicting what a brand outcome will be, to building the bidding and control algorithms that optimize for it, to proving the lift through experimentation. You will work alongside senior scientists and engineers, applying advances in machine learning, online optimization, optimal control, forecasting, and causal inference. You will also join the Amazon science community, with opportunities to publish papers, attend workshops and conferences, and gain early access to Amazon ML technologies.  
  
Key job responsibilities  
In this role, you will work with a highly motivated team of ML scientists and engineers focused on making brand advertising measurable and optimizable against real outcomes. As an Applied Scientist II, you will:  
  

* Contribute to outcome-driven brand optimization, helping define, predict, and bid toward brand outcomes across channels.
* Build prediction models that estimate a customer's likelihood to progress through the funnel, and integrate them into bidding systems.
* Develop the optimization and control algorithms that turn outcome predictions into bids.
* Own projects end to end: frame the problem and success metrics, build and validate prototypes, partner with engineers to productionize, and prove impact through offline analysis and online A/B experimentation.
* Help establish scalable, automated processes for training, monitoring, and feedback so outcome optimization stays reliable and performant at scale.
* Contribute to the science bar on the team through design and model reviews.

**BASIC QUALIFICATIONS**
------------------------

* 3+ years of building models for business application experience
* PhD, or Master's degree and 4+ years of CS, CE, ML or related field experience
* Experience programming in Java, C++, Python or related language
* Experience in designing experiments and statistical analysis of results

jobs.description:
**DESCRIPTION**
---------------

AWS Insights & Optimization is looking for an Applied Scientist to help develop sophisticated algorithms and models that involve analyzing and learning from over 540 billion customer cost, usage, and utilization events daily. We use this data to power cost anomaly detection, cost forecasting, rightsizing recommendations across seven compute services, Savings Plans optimization, and AI-powered conversational experiences that help customers understand and optimize their AWS spend. Our team's vision is to be the world's provider of intelligent AWS cloud financial management, where customers can understand, control, and optimize usage of AWS products. We sit at the nexus of all AWS services and interact directly with end-customers, building relationships with teams across AWS to ensure we offer a secure and reliable experience that builds trust and provides intelligent insights.  
  
As a successful Applied Scientist in AWS Insights & Optimization, you will own models end-to-end — from problem formulation through experimentation to production deployment. Your work may span cost anomaly detection (decomposition, detection, and root cause attribution), time-series forecasting with a focus on accuracy and consistency, rightsizing engines for EC2, EBS, Lambda, ECS, RDS, and Aurora, LLM evaluation science for AI-powered agent experiences, or agent memory architectures that enable persistent, adaptive behavior across sessions. You will work closely with applied scientists, software engineers, and product teams to enhance existing models and build new ones that solve challenging customer problems. You will drive implementation of proposed models, establish testing strategies to validate them before and after production, and define evaluation metrics that determine whether capabilities meet the quality bar. We value accuracy over speed, measurability over intuition, and simplicity over complexity — the simplest model that meets the bar wins. You are an analytical problem solver who enjoys diving into data, are excited about investigating and developing algorithms, and can influence technical teams and business stakeholders to solve real-world customer problems.

* 3+ years of building models for business application experience

jobs.title: Product Engineer - Onboarding Automation
jobs.description:
**About Stuut**
===============

Stuut is the AI coworker that runs order-to-cash for the world’s leading enterprises. Across order management, credit, collections, payments, cash application, disputes and deductions, Stuut does the work end to end and keeps going until the cash hits the bank.

Over 150 companies, spanning the mid-market to the Fortune 50, including Honeywell, ZoomInfo and PerkinElmer, use Stuut to unlock up to 40% more cash flow and cut DSO by 47%. More than $3 billion has moved through the platform to date.

Founded in New York by Tarek Alaruri and Ben Winter, Stuut has raised $93 million from Insight Partners, Andreessen Horowitz, M12, Microsoft’s Venture Fund, and others. Learn more at stuut.ai.

**The Role**
------------

We're hiring our first Product Engineer dedicated to customer onboarding. Your job is to make bringing a new customer live on Stuut faster and smoother, and to build the tools our Forward Deployed Engineering (FDE) team uses on every implementation.

Every new customer brings its own ERP, data, email templates, and collections process. You'll work alongside our FDEs, find the steps that can be automated, and ship the tools that make each onboarding faster than the last: a smarter intake form and the APIs behind it, and agents that turn a customer's existing collateral into a configured account.

This work also lays the foundation for channel partners to implement Stuut for their own clients.

**What Success Looks Like**
---------------------------

Within your first quarter, you've shipped an onboarding automation used on live customers. Within 12 months, customers go live meaningfully faster, your tooling is a core part of every implementation, and it's robust enough for channel partners to use.

**What You'll Do**
------------------

* **Build the intake-to-configuration path:** Turn our intake form into a full product, with the APIs behind it so customer inputs configure an account end to end.
* **Ship agents for onboarding:** Build LLM-powered tools that turn customer collateral (email templates, collection playbooks, process docs) into working Stuut configuration.
* **Make customer data easy:** Make ERP data, flat-file, and schema mapping fast and reliable, whether that means building or integrating the right tool.
* **Improve the onboarding toolkit:** Continuously improve the tools and automation our FDEs use on every implementation.
* **Find the bottleneck, ship the simple fix:** Work with FDEs and customers, measure where time goes, and ship the smallest thing that moves it before building the big thing.
* **Build for partners:** Design onboarding tooling that channel partners can use too.
* **Build with agents:** Use coding agents daily to ship quickly, while owning the testing and debugging of what they produce.

**You Might Be a Fit If You…**
------------------------------

* **Ship real LLM features:** You've built agents, tool use, and prompt/eval loops that run in production, not just demos.
* **Build APIs and backends:** You're comfortable designing APIs that take structured input and configure a system end to end, in a large existing codebase.
* **Handle messy data:** You've worked with ERP data, flat files, schema mapping, validation, and cleaning. ETL experience is a plus.
* **Have product sense:** You can talk to internal users and customers, find the biggest bottleneck, and ship the simplest fix first.
* **Work autonomously:** You scope your own projects once given priorities, and you're comfortable being the first person in a function that may grow into a team.
* **Work agent-native:** You use coding agents every day and can explain and stand behind their output.

**Suggested background:** 5+ years as a software engineer, with time in backend, full-stack, or forward deployed roles at a B2B SaaS or fintech company. We weigh shipped work and judgment over any specific title.

**Bonus Points**
----------------

* You've worked as a forward deployed, implementation, or solutions engineer.
* You've built B2B SaaS onboarding, or worked in fintech, AR/AP, or ERP.
* You've built tools that partners or customers use to implement a product themselves.

**US Compensation**

* Top-of-market salary and equity package
* Benefits (for U.S.-based full-time employees)
* Medical, dental & vision insurance coverage for you
* 401(k) & Match
* Equity
* Flexible PTO
* Parental Leave

**Stuut is an equal opportunity employer committed to building a team with diverse backgrounds, perspectives, and experiences. We do not discriminate based on race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, national origin, age, disability, veteran status, genetic information, or any other characteristic protected by applicable law.**

We are also committed to providing reasonable accommodations throughout the application and interview process. If you need any accommodations, please do not hesitate to reach out.

jobs.description:
**About Manifest**
==================

Manifest OS is the leading AI-native company on a mission to replace the billable hour and make legal services more accessible for American businesses and consumers. We power the next generation of AI-native law firms with one unified global brand, a proprietary technology platform, and a centralized back office — enabling lawyers to eliminate the administrative burden and focus on delivering exceptional outcomes for their clients. Manifest OS has raised a $60M Series A from Menlo Ventures, Kleiner Perkins, First Round, and Quiet Capital.

**About the Role**
------------------

Manifest is building its B2B attorney-facing product from the ground up, and we're looking for a technical, product-minded builder to own it. You'll build and evolve the Portal and Command Center, the core products attorneys use to manage cases, interact with AI-powered workflows, and deliver legal services.

This is a hands-on, 0 1 role for someone who can move between understanding user problems, designing technical solutions, and building and shipping AI-native product experiences. You'll work closely with Engineering, Operations, Sales, and Legal to turn complex workflows into intuitive products that attorneys actively use.

**What You'll Do**
------------------

* Own the end-to-end development of the attorney-facing Portal and Command Center, from identifying problems to building and shipping solutions
* Design and build AI-native features that read, analyze, and generate case-related work using LLMs and agentic systems
* Work hands-on with AI coding tools and agents to prototype, test, and ship product functionality
* Translate complex legal and operational workflows into intuitive product experiences
* Work directly with attorneys and internal teams to understand user needs, gather feedback, and iterate quickly
* Partner closely with Engineering to define technical requirements, evaluate tradeoffs, and bring product ideas to life
* Build and improve integrations, data models, and underlying workflows that power the attorney experience
* Define product metrics, measure adoption and performance, and use data to guide product decisions

**What We're Looking For**
--------------------------

* Experience building and shipping products in a 0 1 environment, ideally at a high-growth B2B company
* Strong technical foundation, with the ability to understand system architecture, data models, APIs, and integrations
* Hands-on experience building AI-native products using LLMs, AI agents, and modern AI development tools
* Comfortable using AI coding tools to prototype, build, and iterate on working product experiences
* Experience translating complex user problems into technical solutions and shipped products
* Strong product instincts and ability to balance user experience, technical complexity, and business impact
* Familiarity with LLM evaluation, testing, and reliability in production environments
* Ability to work across Engineering, Operations, Sales, and Legal in a fast-moving environment
* Bachelor's degree or equivalent practical work experience

**This Is for You If...**
-------------------------

You’re a hands-on builder who enjoys working at the intersection of product and engineering. The focus is on prototyping and shipping solutions rather than spending weeks writing specs. Success requires comfort with ambiguity, a strong connection to users, and the ability to take a product from initial concept through adoption and scale.

**This Is Not for You If...**
-----------------------------

You prefer a traditional product management approach, with a focus on defining requirements and handing execution off to Engineering. This role requires a willingness to get hands-on with AI tools, technical systems, and rapid prototyping, as well as an interest in shaping the roadmap rather than working from an established one.

Compensation Range: $200K - $250K

jobs.title: Forward Deployed Engineer, Evals
jobs.description:
**About David AI**
------------------

At David AI, our vision is to bring impactful AI into billions of lives through voice. Our mission is to help the world's leading AI companies build better voice models and agents. We're building the data and evaluation infrastructure behind those models.

Founded in 2024, we're a fast-growing Series B company backed by NVIDIA, Meritech, First Round, YC, and others, with ~70 people across San Francisco and New York City.

**About this role**
-------------------

We're building David AI's first **Forward Deployed Evals** team. Voice models can only improve on what someone can measure, and most of what matters in voice has never been measured well. This team finds those gaps with our customers and builds the evals to close them.

As a **Forward Deployed Engineer, Evals**, you'll be the primary partner to a set of customers' research teams. In a typical week, you might spot a regression in the latest model checkpoint and design a targeted eval for it, build it end-to-end, calibrate findings against human ratings, and follow through to ensure the model improves.

This is a builder role that is intentionally cross-functional, requiring you to be capable across GTM, Ops, Product, Research, and Engineering to deliver on outcomes.

**In this role, you will**
--------------------------

* Be the evaluation partner to research teams at the world's leading AI labs: learn what they're trying to fix in their voice models, and find what they haven't thought to measure yet.
* Dig into human and automated eval results, pin down exactly where and why a model fails, and decide which failures deserve a dedicated eval.
* Go from idea to working eval in days, independently building whatever the problem calls for: human data pipelines, detectors trained on human labels, or synthetic test harnesses.
* Make every number defensible: an eval you ship should track what people actually hear, and it should hold up when a senior researcher pushes on it.
* Tell research leads what to focus on in their next checkpoint and why, with the data to back it up.
* Productize what works, or turn it into a playbook the team can repeat.
* Shape how forward deployed evals work at David AI as one of the first people on the team.

**Your background looks like**
------------------------------

* 2-7+ years of experience as a technical builder across engineering, product, operations, and research (we're hiring at multiple levels); this might have been as a forward deployed engineer, applied data scientist, ML engineer, product manager, management consultant, or something else entirely.
* You're exceptional at building with AI agents, and you've personally built at least one ambitious thing you can walk us through in detail.
* You move fast. You solve problems in days that might take someone else a month, and you own ambiguous, high-stakes work end to end.
* Strong, demonstrated analytical chops: experiment design, statistics, and knowing whether a metric actually captures what you care about.
* Strong customer presence: you have the credibility and clear communication to earn the trust of technical customers and senior stakeholders.
* Excited to work in person in San Francisco or New York.

**Bonus points if you have**
----------------------------

* Been a founder, or founding engineer/PM/etc. at a startup.
* Experience with speech, audio, or voice models.
* Built or published a benchmark you can share with us.
* Experience working with human raters, annotation, or data-labeling workflows.
* Worked at an AI data or evals company.

**Benefits**
------------

* Unlimited PTO.
* Top-notch health, dental, and vision coverage with 100% coverage for most plans.
* FSA & HSA access.
* 401k access.
* Meals 2x daily through DoorDash + snacks and beverages available at the office.
* Unlimited company-sponsored Barry's classes.

new_jobs.description:
**DESCRIPTION**
---------------

If you are interested in this position, please apply on Twitch's Career site https://www.twitch.tv/jobs/en/If you are interested in this position, please apply on Twitch's Career site https://www.twitch.tv/jobs/en/  
  
About Us  
Twitch is the world’s biggest live streaming service, with global communities built around gaming, entertainment, music, sports, cooking, and more. It is where thousands of communities come together for whatever, every day.  
We’re about community, inside and out. You’ll find coworkers who are eager to team up, collaborate, and smash (or elegantly solve) problems together. We’re on a quest to empower live communities, so if this sounds good to you, see what we’re up to on LinkedIn and X, and discover the projects we’re solving on our Blog. Be sure to explore our Interviewing Guide to learn how to ace our interview process.  
  
About the Role  
  
We're looking for a data scientist with strong statistics and modeling skills to be the science partner for the machine learning and recommendation systems behind Twitch's discovery products. You will work with product managers, ML engineers and applied scientists to help build what our recommendation systems should optimize for. That means balancing what a viewer does today (a click, a play, minutes watched) against what keeps them coming back: return visits, daily habits, and lasting connections with creators. It also means weighing short-form clips against long-form live content, and each surface against the others. This role will draw from a variety of statistical learning techniques, causal inference, optimization and recommender systems evaluation, and it still owns the full path from question to decision.  
  
  
Reporting to the Director of Data Science, you will work from our San Francisco, CA office.  
  
You Will  

* Help define the objective functions and success metrics for ranking and recommendations across feeds, search and notifications. Make the trade-offs explicit between short-term engagement (clicks, plays, watch time) and long-term outcomes (return visits, retention, new creator connections), including how short-form clips and live content add to or take away from each other.
* Evaluate ranking, recommendation and feed changes with ML engineers and applied scientists. This covers A/B tests and long-running holdouts, offline metrics that predict online results, and the cost and value of exploration and cold start. Handle the hard cases: novelty effects, interference between experiments, two-sided marketplace effects involving creators and viewers, and feedback loops in recommendation data.
* Build statistical and ML models that explain viewer behavior and size opportunities, such as propensity, uplift, survival and retention models. Include proxy metrics that predict long-term retention, so teams can decide in days rather than months.
* Turn ambiguous product questions into clear analyses. Quantify the uncertainty, and make recommendations that inform the machine learning and discovery roadmap.
* Define the logging and data needed to measure discovery surfaces, and check its quality.
* Contribute to the team's standards for experimentation, causal inference and model evaluation, and share what you learn with other data scientists.

  
Perks  

* Medical, Dental, Vision & Disability Insurance
* 401(k)
* Maternity & Parental Leave
* Flexible PTO
* Amazon Employee Discount

  
About the team  
Twitch is all about community, and our Community team is a core pillar of what makes Twitch, Twitch. Community Discovery & ML (CDML) helps millions of viewers find the creators and communities they'll love. That covers search, browse, the mobile live and clips feeds, recommended notifications, and the recommendation systems behind them. When a viewer finds a new creator through one of these, it's often the start of a lasting connection. That connection is what keeps viewers, and the creators they watch, coming back.

**BASIC QUALIFICATIONS**
------------------------

* 3+ years of data scientist experience
* A BA/BS in Statistics, Mathematics, Computer Science, Economics, Data Science or a related quantitative field, or equivalent industry experience.
* 3+ years as a data scientist in a high-velocity, data-driven environment, with hands-on experience applying statistical modeling and machine learning (regression, classification, causal inference, time series), including the assumptions behind each method and when it fails.
* Experience designing and analyzing online experiments, including variance reduction, power analysis and the pitfalls of interpreting results.
* Expert SQL and proficiency in Python or R.
* A track record of using data and models to influence product decisions and leadership.

**PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS**
----------------------------

* An MS or PhD in a quantitative field.
* Experience with recommender systems, search ranking or feed ranking, such as offline evaluation (precision and recall, NDCG), exploration versus exploitation, or cold-start problems.
* Experience with multi-objective optimization or with defining objective functions for ranking systems, including choosing weights between competing goals.
* Experience building proxy metrics for long-term outcomes, or estimating long-term effects from long-running holdouts or observational data (e.g., difference-in-differences, synthetic control, uplift modeling).
* Experience with two-sided platforms or marketplaces, where changes for viewers also affect creators or supply.
* Experience on a consumer content platform: streaming, short-form video, social or marketplaces.
* Familiarity with Twitch, as a viewer or a creator (or both!).

They want their investment across Streaming TV, online video, and display to drive measurable business outcomes, from consideration through to purchase and long-term loyalty. The core scientific challenge is connecting a brand ad exposure today to an outcome that may happen days or weeks later, and then optimizing for it in real time.  
  
The Brand Outcomes Optimization team exists to solve that challenge. We build machine-learned models that predict how likely a customer is to move along the full funnel, from awareness through conversion, and we integrate those predictions into real-time bidding so that every brand bid is placed on the opportunity most likely to produce the outcome the advertiser cares about. These systems operate at large scale, and even small improvements to how we predict and optimize for outcomes have meaningful and immediate impact on advertiser results.  
  
As an Applied Scientist II, you will help drive this outcome-optimization. You will take on increasingly ambiguous problems, from predicting what a brand outcome will be, to building the bidding and control algorithms that optimize for it, to proving the lift through experimentation. You will work alongside senior scientists and engineers, applying advances in machine learning, online optimization, optimal control, forecasting, and causal inference. You will also join the Amazon science community, with opportunities to publish papers, attend workshops and conferences, and gain early access to Amazon ML technologies.  
  
Key job responsibilities  
In this role, you will work with a highly motivated team of ML scientists and engineers focused on making brand advertising measurable and optimizable against real outcomes. As an Applied Scientist II, you will:  
  

* Contribute to outcome-driven brand optimization, helping define, predict, and bid toward brand outcomes across channels.
* Build prediction models that estimate a customer's likelihood to progress through the funnel, and integrate them into bidding systems.
* Develop the optimization and control algorithms that turn outcome predictions into bids.
* Own projects end to end: frame the problem and success metrics, build and validate prototypes, partner with engineers to productionize, and prove impact through offline analysis and online A/B experimentation.
* Help establish scalable, automated processes for training, monitoring, and feedback so outcome optimization stays reliable and performant at scale.
* Contribute to the science bar on the team through design and model reviews.

* 3+ years of building models for business application experience
* PhD, or Master's degree and 4+ years of CS, CE, ML or related field experience
* Experience programming in Java, C++, Python or related language
* Experience in designing experiments and statistical analysis of results

**PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS**
----------------------------

* Experience in state-of-the-art deep learning models architecture design and deep learning training and optimization and model pruning

We unite caring with discovery to help make life better for people around the world, knowing that every decision, every detail, and every day matters. Platform Engineering & Integration

### **The Position**

Why Genentech

  
  

A healthier future. It’s what drives us to innovate. To continuously advance science and ensure everyone has access to the healthcare they need today and for generations to come. Creating a world where we all have more time with the people we love. That’s what makes us Genentech.

  
  

We are seeking a machine learning scientist to join our Computational Sciences Center of Excellence as a Postdoctoral Fellow. A successful candidate will conduct cutting-edge research at the intersection of machine learning, biology, and drug development. This position offers a unique opportunity to be jointly mentored by experienced machine learning and computational scientists, with close collaboration across Genentech’s research organization.

  
  

**The Opportunity:**

new_jobs.title: Forward Deployed Engineer, Defense
new_jobs.description:
Navi captures everything a pilot sees and hears and turns it into automated debrief intelligence, sortie-level awareness that has never existed before. You're building the platform that makes that happen.

Navi is live at the U.S. Air Force Test Pilot School, Embry-Riddle, United Aviate, Sling Pilot Academy and Delta State University. You'll take it to the next squadron, the next schoolhouse and the next aircraft.

**On site with customers 30 to 50% of the time · U.S. citizenship required**

**About the role**
==================

In a military flying unit, Navi is the data off every sortie, a debrief waiting when the crew walks in, and the picture instructors and commanders run training, readiness and safety on. Forward deployed engineers make that work at each unit.

You'll spend real time on base with aircrew, instructors, maintainers and commanders. Then you'll write the production code that turns what you learned into product. Not a prototype, not a slide deck: the same codebase every customer runs. You'll own a deployment end to end, from the data coming off the aircraft to the people acting on it.

**Problems you'll own**
=======================

**Get the data off the aircraft.** A sortie lands as recorder files, mission data cartridges, cockpit video and audio, sitting on government computers and removable media. Each has its own format, sampling rate and clock, and its own traps: a time code with no year, a clock that was never set, an altitude that follows the altimeter setting. You'll build the converters and the uploader that runs unattended on an operations desk, and line every source up to the same instant.

**Make the debrief one an instructor would sign.** A unit's training lives in syllabi, gradesheets, maneuver guides and instructor standards. You'll turn those into events, tolerances and rubrics a sortie can be held to, and build the tools instructors use to keep them current. Then you'll prove it works: grades checked against the instructors' own, and every finding tied to the data and the document behind it.

**Build what commanders run the unit on.** Where each student stands in the syllabus and who is falling behind, upcoming evaluations and checkrides, instructor workload, aircraft availability. You'll find the question a squadron commander or director of operations asks every week and make Navi answer it.

**See safety across the whole fleet.** Every exceedance, unstable approach and trend across every sortie, not only the ones someone wrote up. You'll turn flight data into a safety picture a unit can act on before something happens.

**Put the unit's knowledge one question away.** Regulations, syllabi, maneuver guides and lessons learned are spread across hundreds of documents. You'll build the assistant that answers from them and from the unit's own flight data, with a citation behind every answer.

**Deploy where the mission is.** Controlled unclassified information, restricted networks, government computers without admin rights, older hardware, MFA, audit trails and accreditation. You'll build to those constraints from day one, make a 3D replay run smoothly on a five-year-old government laptop, and help write the security documentation that goes with it.

**Close the loop.** Aircrew and instructors rate debriefs, flag findings and correct transcripts. You'll turn that into fixes that ship the same week, and into patterns the product team builds for every customer.

**About you**
=============

* 3+ years shipping production software, in any programming language. You've owned a system in production end to end.
* You're at home in messy real-world data: file formats, sampling rates, clock alignment, units, sensor faults, missing channels.
* Comfortable below the application. You can stand up an environment, read an access policy and debug a service that won't start.
* You can sit with aircrew, an instructor or a commander and come back with the right problem, not just the one they named.
* You build with AI coding agents every day, and you know how to check their work: tests, measurements and a second look before anything ships.
* You're comfortable owning outcomes when the roadmap isn't written yet.
* U.S. citizen, able to travel to bases regularly.

**Nice to have**
================

* Military aviation experience: aircrew, instructor, maintainer, flight test or safety
* Flight training or standardization and evaluation (Stan/Eval) in a flying unit
* Military flight data: mission data recorders, IRIG time code, IRIG 106 Chapter 10, MIL-STD-1553
* Aviation safety programs such as MFOQA
* Security and accreditation work: NIST 800-171, CMMC, RMF or an ATO package
* An active security clearance
* Signal processing, computer vision on cockpit video, or speech-to-text on cockpit audio

**What this role is not**
=========================

Not a sales engineer running demos. Not support working a ticket queue. Not a consultant handing over a report. You write production code that ships to every customer, and you're the reason it works where it lands.

**Why this role matters**
=========================

Every sortie is expensive, and much of what it records is never reviewed. Navi turns each one into a debrief in about a minute and puts what a unit learns in front of the people who make decisions about aircrew, aircraft and safety. The bar is a debrief an instructor would sign and a picture a commander would act on. As the engineer in the room, you're the one who gets it there.

**What you'll get**
===================

* Early-stage equity: real ownership in a category-defining company
* Flight training: earn your pilot's license and build with true domain expertise
* Time on the flight line with the people who use what you build
* A role that grows into leading Navi's defense engineering as we scale

===============

**About Stuut**
===============

Stuut is the AI coworker that runs order-to-cash for the world’s leading enterprises. Across order management, credit, collections, payments, cash application, disputes and deductions, Stuut does the work end to end and keeps going until the cash hits the bank.

Over 150 companies, spanning the mid-market to the Fortune 50, including Honeywell, ZoomInfo and PerkinElmer, use Stuut to unlock up to 40% more cash flow and cut DSO by 47%. More than $3 billion has moved through the platform to date.

Founded in New York by Tarek Alaruri and Ben Winter, Stuut has raised $93 million from Insight Partners, Andreessen Horowitz, M12, Microsoft’s Venture Fund, and others. Learn more at stuut.ai.

**The Role**
------------

We're hiring our first Product Engineer dedicated to customer onboarding. Your job is to make bringing a new customer live on Stuut faster and smoother, and to build the tools our Forward Deployed Engineering (FDE) team uses on every implementation.

Every new customer brings its own ERP, data, email templates, and collections process. You'll work alongside our FDEs, find the steps that can be automated, and ship the tools that make each onboarding faster than the last: a smarter intake form and the APIs behind it, and agents that turn a customer's existing collateral into a configured account.

This work also lays the foundation for channel partners to implement Stuut for their own clients.

**What Success Looks Like**
---------------------------

Within your first quarter, you've shipped an onboarding automation used on live customers. Within 12 months, customers go live meaningfully faster, your tooling is a core part of every implementation, and it's robust enough for channel partners to use.

**What You'll Do**
------------------

* **Build the intake-to-configuration path:** Turn our intake form into a full product, with the APIs behind it so customer inputs configure an account end to end.
* **Ship agents for onboarding:** Build LLM-powered tools that turn customer collateral (email templates, collection playbooks, process docs) into working Stuut configuration.
* **Make customer data easy:** Make ERP data, flat-file, and schema mapping fast and reliable, whether that means building or integrating the right tool.
* **Improve the onboarding toolkit:** Continuously improve the tools and automation our FDEs use on every implementation.
* **Find the bottleneck, ship the simple fix:** Work with FDEs and customers, measure where time goes, and ship the smallest thing that moves it before building the big thing.
* **Build for partners:** Design onboarding tooling that channel partners can use too.
* **Build with agents:** Use coding agents daily to ship quickly, while owning the testing and debugging of what they produce.

**You Might Be a Fit If You…**
------------------------------

* **Ship real LLM features:** You've built agents, tool use, and prompt/eval loops that run in production, not just demos.
* **Build APIs and backends:** You're comfortable designing APIs that take structured input and configure a system end to end, in a large existing codebase.
* **Handle messy data:** You've worked with ERP data, flat files, schema mapping, validation, and cleaning. ETL experience is a plus.
* **Have product sense:** You can talk to internal users and customers, find the biggest bottleneck, and ship the simplest fix first.
* **Work autonomously:** You scope your own projects once given priorities, and you're comfortable being the first person in a function that may grow into a team.
* **Work agent-native:** You use coding agents every day and can explain and stand behind their output.

**Suggested background:** 5+ years as a software engineer, with time in backend, full-stack, or forward deployed roles at a B2B SaaS or fintech company. We weigh shipped work and judgment over any specific title.

**Bonus Points**
----------------

* You've worked as a forward deployed, implementation, or solutions engineer.
* You've built B2B SaaS onboarding, or worked in fintech, AR/AP, or ERP.
* You've built tools that partners or customers use to implement a product themselves.

* 401(k) & Match
* Equity
* Flexible PTO

**The role**
============

As an inference infrastructure engineer, you’ll build and operate the systems that deploy Applied Compute’s models and serve production inference traffic. You’ll own model deployment, GPU capacity management, request routing, and recovery from failures, balancing reliability, latency, and serving efficiency. You’ll partner with research engineers to support new models and with inference performance engineers to bring execution improvements into production. Your work will make it possible to release models safely, securely, and serve changing workloads reliably.

**What You’ll Do**

* Design, build, and maintain the inference APIs developers use to interact with our models, supporting streaming responses, tool use, structured outputs, and multimodal inputs.

**About David AI**
------------------

At David AI, our vision is to bring impactful AI into billions of lives through voice. Our mission is to help the world's leading AI companies build better voice models and agents. We're building the data and evaluation infrastructure behind those models.

Founded in 2024, we're a fast-growing Series B company backed by NVIDIA, Meritech, First Round, YC, and others, with ~70 people across San Francisco and New York City.

**About this role**
-------------------

We're building David AI's first **Forward Deployed Evals** team. Voice models can only improve on what someone can measure, and most of what matters in voice has never been measured well. This team finds those gaps with our customers and builds the evals to close them.

As a **Forward Deployed Engineer, Evals**, you'll be the primary partner to a set of customers' research teams. In a typical week, you might spot a regression in the latest model checkpoint and design a targeted eval for it, build it end-to-end, calibrate findings against human ratings, and follow through to ensure the model improves.

This is a builder role that is intentionally cross-functional, requiring you to be capable across GTM, Ops, Product, Research, and Engineering to deliver on outcomes.

--------------------------

* Be the evaluation partner to research teams at the world's leading AI labs: learn what they're trying to fix in their voice models, and find what they haven't thought to measure yet.

* Go from idea to working eval in days, independently building whatever the problem calls for: human data pipelines, detectors trained on human labels, or synthetic test harnesses.
* Make every number defensible: an eval you ship should track what people actually hear, and it should hold up when a senior researcher pushes on it.
* Tell research leads what to focus on in their next checkpoint and why, with the data to back it up.
